newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on wetter weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on wetter weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on wetter weather in portions of the U.S. corn growing region plus forecasts for more rain, traders said.
"The rains over the weekend, calls for more in the next few days, and rain for this weekend drove it sharply lower," a trader said.
Meteorologists said rains fell over roughly one half of central Illinois and more precipitation was expected.
"In our estimation, the dry area of central Illinois is a heck of a lot smaller than it was Friday," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis.

Dry soils in portions of the Midwest, especially in central and western Illinois, had been keeping the market on edge. Traders were expecting a decline Monday in the condition rating for the U.S. corn crop due to the hotter and drier weather last week in portions of the key U.S. corn growing region. USDA late Monday was expected to release its updated weekly crop briefs based on conditions in place as of Sunday.
Commercial selling weighed on prices but fund buying of roughly 20 million bushels limited losses, traders said.
Corn closed 2-1/2 to 7-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down 7-1/4 at $2.45-1/4.

In spread trading, Tenco Inc did four million bushels of September/March at 8-1/2 to nine cents, premium March, traders said. Farmers Commodities Corp spread one million September/December at 1-1/4 cents, premium December, traders said.

Continental Grain sold six million bushels of December and Iowa Grain sold four million bushels of December, traders said. Term Commodities bought 10 million bushels of December and Refco Inc bought seven million December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 63,000 contracts, below the 74,159 traded Friday.

In corn options, FIMAT Futures sold 1,000 December $2.60 calls at eight cents, Griffin Trading bought 500 December $2.60 puts at 23-1/2 cents and LIT America sold 500 September $2.60 calls at 2-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 25,000 contracts, below the 36,664 traded Friday.
